messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Meze sur la vojo de nia vivo Mi trovis min en malluma arbaro, ĉar la prava vojo estis perdita.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG] After the table, list any MISSING or WRONG items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Esperanto) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | **Nel** | preposition + definite article “in the” (locative) | **Meze** | “midway” (contains the idea of “in the middle”) | **WRONG** (does not render the simple locative “in”) | | **mezzo** | noun “middle” (the exact midpoint) | **Meze** | “midway” | **OK** | | **del** | genitive “of the” linking “cammin” to “vita” | **de** | “of” | **OK** | | **cammin** | noun “road, path” (the journey) | **vojo** | “road” | **OK** | | **di** | preposition “of” (possessive) | **de** | “of” | **OK** | | **nostra** | possessive adjective “our” (collective) | **nia** | “our” | **OK** | | **vita** | noun “life” (the span of existence) | **vivo** | “life” | **OK** | | **mi** | reflexive pronoun “myself” (object of “ritrovai”) | **Mi** | “I” (subject) | **OK** | | **ritrovai** | verb “found (myself)” (past remote) | **trovis** | “found” | **OK** | | **per** | preposition “within, through” (locative) | **en** | “in/within” | **OK** | | **una** | indefinite article “a” (introducing “selva”) | — | — | **MISSING** (Esperanto has no indefinite article) | | **selva** | noun “forest, wood” | **arbaro** | “forest” | **OK** | | **oscura** | adjective “dark” | **malluma** | “dark” | **OK** | | **ché** | conjunction “for, because” (causal) | **ĉar** | “because/for” | **OK** | | **la** | definite article “the” | **la** | “the” | **OK** | | **diritta** | adjective “right, straight, correct” | **prava** | “right/correct” | **OK** | | **via** | noun “way, path” | **vojo** | “way” | **OK** | | **era** | imperfect of “to be” – “had been” | **estis** | “was / had been” | **OK** | | **smarrita** | past participle “lost, missed” | **perdita** | “lost / missed” | **OK** |
---
### Items Needing Attention - **Nel** – marked **WRONG**: the Esperanto “Meze” conveys “midway” but does not directly express the locative preposition “in”. A more literal rendering would be “En la mezo …”. - **una** – marked **MISSING**: Esperanto does not use an indefinite article; the translation omits it, which is acceptable in Esperanto but noted as a missing token for a strict one‑to‑one mapping.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING or WRONG items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Output per line: Line #, Original Translation, Issues, Corrected Translation (if any). Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
